steps.text: For the custard: In a small saucepan, combine 1/2 cup sugar, 5 tablespoons flour and a pinch of salt. Stir in milk, a little at a time, until smooth. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Boil 60 seconds, then pour a small amount of hot liquid into the 2 egg yolks, and stir. Then return now heated egg yolks to saucepan and stir, over heat, until mixture starts to bubble again. Remove from heat, add vanilla. Cover and chill in refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).

For the pastry: In a medium saucepan, combine shortening and water and bring to a boil. Sift together 1 cup flour and a pinch of salt and pour all at once into boiling mixture. Stir vigorously until mixture forms a ball. Remove from heat, and add eggs, one at a time, stirring vigorously after each addition. Drop by spoonfuls onto baking sheet, or pipe into desired shape.
Bake 10 minutes in the preheated oven, then reduce heat to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) and bake 25 minutes more, or until golden. Cool completely, split, fill with custard, and replace tops.

review.reviewBody: I ran thru all the cream puff recipes here and found that they are all the same. What makes or breaks the puff pastry is the way you make them. I use a turbo roaster for baking and I find that the puffs would stay in shape better if I bake them at 450F for the first 20 mins, then 350 for the next 5 mins, then 250 for the last 5 mins. This way the puffs are cooked inside (it taste less eggy, if the insides aren't cooked they look and taste like scrambled eggs). As for those who said that their pastry didn't puff, i think you better check the temp, lower temp won't help the pastry puff, it also causes you're dough to be soaked in butter (deep fried dough as my brother called it)as i've experienced.

This came out perfect! I love the custard as it is not too sweet nor is it bland. I followed the advise of another reviewer who baked it at 450 for 20 minutes 350 for 5 minutes and 250 for 5 minutes. In my batch I tripled it and it made about 80 cream puffs with way too much custard left over. I used a teaspoon to measure out the puffs and then again to fill with the custard. I also melted chocolate and put it into a sandwich bag, cut a small piece of the corner off and then squeezed the chocolate on top of them in a zig zag pattern. I put them pack in the fridge to harden. I then took them out and dusted with confectioners sugar. The chocolate makes it!!! This is something to definitely hand on to!

These were so easy, and super delicious! I followed the cooking times/temps recommended by some reviewers, lowering after 15-20 (15 seemed better) minutes to 350 for 5 minutes, and then to 250 for the last 5 minutes. When cooled and filled, I brushed a mixture of melted chocolate/butter on top, then put them in the fridge to harden. Absolutely delicious!

The puff recipe was perfect. I have another recipe I’ve used in the past from a 1960’s cooking text book I had in college that uses the same amount in ingredients but lower oven temperature and longer time. I added a tsp of sugar & almost a tsp of vanilla to the puff for more flavor and used a solid shortening. I filled the puff with whipped cream and macerated strawberries & decorated with fresh, caps on. Beautiful & delicious.

Wow. Just wow. I used butter instead of shortening and 3 eggs instead of 4. These were absolutely amazing. The custard was thick, creamy, and delicious. The pastry was extremely easy to make and came out perfect. I filled a plastic bag with the custard and piped it into the pastries. I didn't have to cut them or anything. I just opened up a little crack on the tops of them and squeezed the custard in. I put a chocolate glaze on half of them. Next time I make them (there will DEFINITELY be a next time) I will frost all of them.

I tried this recipe--and the puffs turned out great---instead of beating by hand I used the electric mixer--I also added dill to flour mixture--going to use crabmeat salad for the filling. I baked them for 20 minutes at 450 then 400 for 10 minutes, 5 minutes at 350 and last 10 minutes at 250--they were so light I could not believe it--I was always scared the puffs would fall(my first ones years ago did and tasted !!!) but this time they were perfect--I will certainly do this again--a regular soup spoon makes them too big (for what I needed) but a heaping teaspoon was just the right size. I used spoons that are for the table not measuring spoons--
Great custard worked really well! I used pepperidge farm sheet if puff pastry cut out circles and baked them-they came out great and shortened the recipe in half!

This recipe is much easier than it sounds. if you've done any kind of cooking or baking, this is recipe is simple and almost foolproof. You can use it for cream puffs or with a few minor changes, for eclairs as well. The only thing is, I made them a bit smaller and came out with 24 instead of the 10 it shows. I like my cream puffs rather bite sized, Of course, this also altered the baking time, but if you thump them on the bottom and they sound hollow, you know they're done.

Excellent recipe - the best cream puffs I've ever made. I followed one reviewers advice and cooked for 20 minutes at 450 degrees, then for 5 minutes at 350 degrees, and then for 5 minutes at 250 degrees - they came out perfect! Thanks!

These turned out great, I used about 3/8th cup coconut oil and 1/8 butter instead of vegetable shortening. I also added some sugar and vanilla to the pastry dough. They were delicious, couldn't stop eating them!
First time making it, and it tasted great!! I would be careful to make tiny dolps of dough, because I had MONSTER CREAM PUFFS! I also liked the 450 degrees for 10, 350 for 5 and 250 for the last 5
YOMMEY IN MY TOMMEY
I put Chocolate pudding in the pastry
I made this twice now. The trick is getting them the right size. Mine were a little smaller and I lost some batter out of the back cause I forgot to tie it off, I learned a lot.
So hard (for beginners) but so fun!!! By the way, DON'T use butter! Especially not salted butter. It was good, though.
This recipe took me back to when my mother made cream puffs with my help. The shells and custard were almost exactly the same as we made 50 years ago. Absolutely the way cream puffs should be!
perfect!

This is the best custard recipe I've come across. The pastry is pretty much the same from one recipe to the next. Made these for dessert with dinner when we had friends over. I served with chocolate sauce, and they got rave reviews from everyone.
First time I've ever attempted anything like this. These were amazing! A huge hit for Sunday football!
Amazing cream puffs! Made them for a softball party and everyone loved them!
